gap_analysis: Real deployed topology, NVFP4, int 5718ef2d89. Decode D3-32 (8 nodes, real EP32): r8/r16/r24 19.10/24.86/29.75 ms vs nvfp4 achievable 9.50/11.46/13.50 (x2.01/2.17/2.20); r24 exposed vs achievable: GEMMs 5.74 vs 2.93, DSA top-k 2.55 vs 0.23, small elementwise 2.02 vs 0.15, DSA q/MLA/DCP 2.68 vs 1.00, KDA core 3.43 vs 1.81, MegaMoE 6.55 vs 5.27, SP comm 1.76 vs 1.28, indexer 0.94 vs 0.43, preview-drafter tail 4.09 vs 0.28. Prefill P3-16 (4 nodes, real DEP16): F16K 790.3 ms = 20.7K tok/s/GPU, F8K 401.4 ms = 20.4K, vs additive achievable 628.2 / 320.4 (x1.26) and model step 532.8 (30.7K); biggest: KDA core 79.8 vs 17.4, router/latent/top-k/norm 80.5 vs 48.0, sparse MLA 49.2 vs 15.4, indexer + top-k 61.6 vs 33.8; MegaMoE 261.5 vs 293.3 (below the model: model pessimistic). Slices calibrated against these: decode target-only x93/24 within 2%, MegaMoE per layer +7%; prefill step x93/24 -2.5%, MegaMoE per layer -13%. Harness root cause fixed early: sdec reads moe.gate.weight in its fused MoE front, so the routing fixture never reached the sdec graph; bench-only expert-count emulation.
inefficiencies: Slice deviation: 24-layer view (896 experts x 93 layers do not fit at EP4); model rows rescaled to the same layer counts
Slice deviation: MegaMoE dispatch/combine over 4 GPUs instead of 32 (decode) / 16 (prefill)
Slice deviation: only the DSpark PREVIEW drafter exists on Lustre (MLA, full-context attention); use target-only numbers or -x
Integration: D-GEMM and EN merged textually clean but broke at import (renamed mxfp8 predicate); fixed on int
plan: Merge landed-ready workstreams into int (int_tests4.sh + NVFP4 slice A/B per merge); D-FUSE (sp_coverage meta device) and P-MOE (re-base on post-D-MOE int) were sent back
Re-run d8/p16 NVFP4 on int at milestones (hold8 queue: one standing request)
Release DSpark drafter on Lustre would remove the preview-drafter tail artifact (needs the user/EN for the checkpoint)
